sanity_expectations: At t=0, dT_c/dt is negative because basal_heat_production < environmental_heat_transfer_coefficient*(T_c-ambient_temperature) and effector_recruitment_state starts at 0; the trajectory initially cools below set point.

effector_recruitment_state should lag behind tanh((T_c-core_temperature_set_point)/feedback_recruitment_temperature_scale), approaching a negative value only after T_c has already fallen below the set point.
Because effector_adjustment_time_constant is not tiny, early-time cooling is closer to passive environmental cooling, with stronger corrective feedback appearing later at similar T_c values.
The heat-capacity denominator remains positive and near order effective_heat_capacity throughout mild excursions; no blow-up or complex values should occur.

With effector_kinetic_asymmetry=0.45 and the inherited initial condition, the dataset mainly probes the below-set-point branch of asymmetric recruitment timing; a full above-vs-below asymmetry comparison is weak or absent unless the trajectory crosses the set point later.

If sampled states reach |T_c-core_temperature_set_point| of order 0.5 C, both tanh recruitment curvature and the state-dependent heat-capacity modulation become visibly active rather than collapsing to their linear limits.

spec.rationale: Preserving the supplied validated ODE-system contract, this dataset should be generated by integrating the two-state system over a recovery window long enough to show delayed thermoeffector recruitment and the sign-dependent kinetics encoded by effector_kinetic_asymmetry. The chosen 0–120 min window with 301 points resolves the early lag phase and the later relaxation. Parameter values keep the denominator positive and moderate over mild physiological excursions, avoid immediate parent-limit collapse, and keep the recruitment nonlinearity active around sub-degree temperature errors because feedback_recruitment_temperature_scale=0.5 C makes order-0.5 C deviations relevant. heat_capacity_temperature_sensitivity=0.3 gives visible but not dominating state-dependent thermal storage. effector_adjustment_time_constant=12 min keeps recruitment delay observable relative to core thermal relaxation. effector_kinetic_asymmetry=0.45 stays within the suggested admissible range and creates a real asymmetry in recruitment timing without risking denominator singularity in the effector-state equation, since 1-0.45*tanh(.) remains positive. Because the inherited initial condition is exactly T_c=core_temperature_set_point and effector_recruitment_state=0, the trajectory starts at the set point with zero recruitment signal; thus the sign-dependent kinetic asymmetry is initially inactive and only becomes observable if the net heat balance moves T_c away from set point. The chosen basal heat production and ambient heat loss do that immediately: at t=0 the net flux is slightly cooling, so the system moves below set point, activating the negative-error branch and then delayed recruitment. This means the present dataset exposes delayed feedback and the below-set-point side of the asymmetric kinetics, but not a full cross-sign comparison unless the trajectory later crosses the set point; that limitation is imposed by the inherited initial state and should be documented rather than repaired. No noise is added; outputs are exact numerical integration results.

spec.scenario_text: Core body temperature is followed after a small thermal perturbation while ambient conditions and activity remain fixed. The target is the instantaneous rate of change of core temperature as metabolic heat production and thermoregulatory heat loss restore a stable operating temperature. The baseline response treats heat-storage capacity as constant and thermoeffector output as an immediate negative-feedback response. This produces a smooth relaxation without requiring skin temperature or effector activity as additional dynamic states.

response_change.parent_relation: The target dT_c_dt is an affine linear function of core temperature error T_c-core_temperature_set_point with one constant thermoregulatory feedback gain, so the restorative slope is the same for small and larger deviations.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same negative-feedback pathway but relax the constant-gain assumption so feedback strength depends on the magnitude of T_c-core_temperature_set_point, producing a nonlinear temperature-error to dT_c_dt mapping.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories started at different initial thermal offsets under the same ambient conditions, larger positive deviations cool back disproportionately faster than predicted by a single linear restorative slope, while near-set-point relaxation remains close to the parent law.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when the initial perturbation is large enough that thermoeffector recruitment is no longer approximately linear in temperature error, yet still within the mild physiological range where one-compartment core temperature remains meaningful and feedback remains stabilizing.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest perturbations may look nearly linear; in holdout with somewhat larger initial deviations but the same fixed ambient and activity conditions, the same mechanism manifests as stronger-than-linear restoration that bends the dT_c_dt versus T_c relation.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the nonlinear modulation of feedback gain to its linear small-signal limit so effective thermoregulatory gain is constant over the observed temperature range.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes thermoregulatory corrective output is exactly proportional to core-temperature error over the whole admissible range, omitting amplitude-dependent recruitment of heat-loss effectors.
plan.baseline_assumption: Thermoregulatory effectors respond without delay and do not saturate in the baseline range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-dependent recruitment of thermoeffector strength makes effective negative-feedback gain depend on the magnitude of core thermal deviation, even without adding delay or extra measured states.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the idealized constant-gain feedback assumption rather than add a wholly new process. The parent target mapping is a single-slope relaxation: with ambient_temperature, basal_heat_production, environmental_heat_transfer_coefficient, and effective_heat_capacity held fixed, varying only T_c changes dT_c_dt linearly. This implies that two perturbations of different size differ only by scale, so one shared parameter set predicts the same local restorative slope everywhere. Physiologically, mild deviations can recruit little additional effector output, while somewhat larger deviations recruit stronger vasomotor and evaporative or other heat-loss responses, making the restoring action increase nonlinearly with error magnitude. The resulting child changes the scored mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory: dT_c_dt as a function of observed T_c gains curvature. A concrete observable contrast is that trajectories starting farther above set point return faster than a linear extrapolation from small perturbations would predict, under the same fixed ambient conditions and activity. This is admissible when initial core offsets vary across experiments or samples; if all observations stay infinitesimally close to set point, the refinement will be hard to identify and the parent remains a good approximation.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when the initial perturbation is large enough that thermoeffector recruitment is no longer approximately linear in temperature error, yet still within the mild physiological range where one-compartment core temperature remains meaningful and feedback remains stabilizing.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest perturbations may look nearly linear; in holdout with somewhat larger initial deviations but the same fixed ambient and activity conditions, the same mechanism manifests as stronger-than-linear restoration that bends the dT_c_dt versus T_c relation.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the nonlinear modulation of feedback gain to its linear small-signal limit so effective thermoregulatory gain is constant over the observed temperature range.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-dependent recruitment of thermoeffector strength makes effective negative-feedback gain depend on the magnitude of core thermal deviation, even without adding delay or extra measured states.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored target mapping from observed T_c to dT_c_dt acquires curvature with a distinct near-set-point weak-response regime and a stronger finite high-error regime. No single constant gain can match both the local small-error slope and the faster restoration at larger deviations under one shared parameter set.
contract.assumption_before: Thermoregulatory effectors respond without delay and do not saturate in the baseline range.
contract.assumption_after: Thermoregulatory effectors still respond immediately, but their recruited strength increases nonlinearly with temperature-error magnitude through a smooth saturating recruitment law.
contract.parent_reduction: When |T_c-core_temperature_set_point| is small relative to feedback_recruitment_temperature_scale over the observed range, tanh((T_c-core_temperature_set_point)/feedback_recruitment_temperature_scale) varies little and the law approaches a single approximately linear restorative relation after local refitting.
contract.observable_signature: With ambient_temperature, basal_heat_production, environmental_heat_transfer_coefficient, and effective_heat_capacity held fixed, plotting dT_c_dt against T_c shows an approximately linear relation near core_temperature_set_point but increasingly steeper cooling for larger positive T_c-core_temperature_set_point. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only any hidden auxiliary trajectory, and is observable across experiments that differ in initial thermal offset while staying in the mild physiological range.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only produce one affine dependence of dT_c_dt on T_c, so after matching near-set-point relaxation it necessarily underpredicts the stronger restoration seen at larger deviations, or after matching large-deviation recovery it overpredicts the local slope near the set point. This mismatch persists across trajectories with different initial offsets under the same ambient conditions because the child changes curvature of the target mapping rather than merely rescaling one coefficient.

range_suggestions.feedback_recruitment_temperature_scale: positive, typically small-to-moderate relative to admissible core-temperature deviations; for mild physiology roughly 0.1 to 2 degrees Celsius

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed effective_heat_capacity, the same net heat flux always produces a temperature-rate change with constant conversion factor, so dT_c_dt is affine in net heat flux apart from the existing feedback nonlinearity.
response_change.child_relation: Make effective thermal storage depend on core temperature so the same net heat flux yields different dT_c_dt at different T_c, changing the local slope and curvature of the T_c-to-dT_c_dt map even when ambient conditions and activity are fixed.
response_change.observable_effect: For comparable positive and negative thermal deviations around the set point, recovery becomes asymmetric in speed: regions with larger effective heat capacity show slower temperature-rate response to the same restoring heat flux magnitude.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when admissible core-temperature excursions are large enough that temperature-dependent tissue heat storage is not negligible relative to the baseline effective_heat_capacity variation scale, while remaining in mild physiological ranges with positive total heat capacity.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, small perturbations near set point can still look close to the parent law; in holdout with somewhat larger but still physiological excursions, the altered temperature-rate curvature appears as systematically slower or faster relaxation than any one constant-capacity fit predicts.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the temperature dependence of effective heat capacity to zero, giving a constant effective_heat_capacity.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes a constant conversion from net heat flux to core-temperature rate, omitting plausible temperature dependence of effective body heat storage over the perturbation range.
plan.baseline_assumption: Effective heat capacity is constant over the modeled range.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-dependent effective heat capacity from changing partition of stored heat among tissues and body water over mild thermal deviations.
plan.rationale: The parent already contains restoring heat production/loss terms, but it enforces a single flux-to-temperature-rate gain through constant effective_heat_capacity. A realistic next refinement is to relax that assumption rather than add a new process. Vary the initial core-temperature perturbation amplitude while holding ambient_temperature, basal_heat_production, environmental_heat_transfer_coefficient, and thermoregulatory_feedback_gain fixed. In the parent, after accounting for the existing feedback nonlinearity, the same net restoring heat flux implies the same temperature-rate conversion everywhere because storage capacity is fixed. In the child, storage capacity changes with T_c, so the slope of dT_c_dt versus net heat flux depends on temperature, producing an observable curvature/asymmetry in relaxation across larger deviations. A single refit of the parent's existing parameters cannot generally match both near-set-point and farther-from-set-point recovery speeds when the discrepancy comes from denominator variation rather than only numerator feedback strength. This is scientifically admissible for mild physiology if the capacity modulation remains positive and moderate; if perturbations are extremely small, the effect collapses toward the parent and may be hard to identify.

response_change.parent_relation: The thermoregulatory correction is an instantaneous static function of the current core-temperature error, so for any observed T_c the target dT_c_dt is uniquely determined with no dependence on recent thermal history.

response_change.observable_effect: After a step-like thermal perturbation, early-time relaxation is weaker than the parent predicts and later-time relaxation strengthens at similar T_c, creating hysteresis in the dT_c_dt versus T_c relationship.

contract.scientific_mechanism: Autonomic and vascular/sudomotor effectors have finite heat-transfer and metabolic adjustment capacity, so recruited effectors cannot generate indefinitely increasing corrective heat flux as core-temperature error grows.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the feedback contribution now depends on a bounded nonlinear modulation of core-temperature error, changing the asymptotic shape of the target mapping while preserving the local near-set-point slope. contract.assumption_before: Thermoregulatory effectors respond without delay and do not saturate in the baseline range.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when initial perturbations or subsequent trajectories cross enough above and below the set point that normalized temperature error has both signs and magnitude not negligible relative to 1, while ambient temperature and activity remain fixed.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, same-sign mild perturbations show a common apparent lag; in holdout with both warming and cooling excursions or larger cross-set-point relaxations, the sign-dependent lag produces asymmetric recovery timing not captured by one shared effector time constant.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when heating and cooling recruitment kinetics are equal, reducing the sign-dependent adjustment back to the original single effector_adjustment_time_constant.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes a single autonomic/vascular recruitment timescale for all thermoegulatory directions, ignoring that effector engagement and withdrawal are often faster for one sign of thermal error than the other.
plan.baseline_assumption: Thermoregulatory effectors respond with one symmetric first-order lag regardless of whether core temperature is above or below the set point.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Direction-dependent thermoeffector recruitment kinetics arising from different physiological pathways for heat-loss versus heat-conservation/production responses.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the symmetric-lag assumption already present in the effector pathway rather than adding an unrelated process. The parent target mapping uses one shared effector_adjustment_time_constant, so after refitting it can only impose one compromise phase lag between T_c deviation and delivered corrective heat flux across both warming and cooling trajectories. Under fixed ambient temperature and activity, if one compares recovery from a small positive temperature perturbation versus a small negative perturbation of similar magnitude, the parent predicts the same recruitment timing up to sign reversal, whereas the child allows asymmetric delay and therefore different early-time slopes and hysteresis in dT_c_dt at matched |T_c-core_temperature_set_point|. This is observable only when the sampled trajectory includes both signs of thermal deviation or crosses the set point; if all observations stay on one side, the refinement may be weakly identifiable and effectively collapse to the parent. Because the omitted feature changes the scored T_c dynamics through the timing of corrective heat flux, not merely an unobserved auxiliary path, it is a consequential target-mapping refinement.

response_change.parent_relation: The target dT_c_dt is an affine linear function of core temperature error T_c-core_temperature_set_point with one constant thermoregulatory feedback gain, so the restorative slope is the same for small and larger deviations.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same negative-feedback pathway but relax the constant-gain assumption so feedback strength depends on the magnitude of T_c-core_temperature_set_point, producing a nonlinear temperature-error to dT_c_dt mapping.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories started at different initial thermal offsets under the same ambient conditions, larger positive deviations cool back disproportionately faster than predicted by a single linear restorative slope, while near-set-point relaxation remains close to the parent law.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when the initial perturbation is large enough that thermoeffector recruitment is no longer approximately linear in temperature error, yet still within the mild physiological range where one-compartment core temperature remains meaningful and feedback remains stabilizing.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest perturbations may look nearly linear; in holdout with somewhat larger initial deviations but the same fixed ambient and activity conditions, the same mechanism manifests as stronger-than-linear restoration that bends the dT_c_dt versus T_c relation.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the nonlinear modulation of feedback gain to its linear small-signal limit so effective thermoregulatory gain is constant over the observed temperature range.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-dependent recruitment of thermoeffector strength makes effective negative-feedback gain depend on the magnitude of core thermal deviation, even without adding delay or extra measured states.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored target mapping from observed T_c to dT_c_dt acquires curvature with a distinct near-set-point weak-response regime and a stronger finite high-error regime. No single constant gain can match both the local small-error slope and the faster restoration at larger deviations under one shared parameter set.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Thermoregulatory effectors respond without delay and do not saturate in the baseline range.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Thermoregulatory effectors still respond immediately, but their recruited strength increases nonlinearly with temperature-error magnitude through a smooth saturating recruitment law.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: When |T_c-core_temperature_set_point| is small relative to feedback_recruitment_temperature_scale over the observed range, tanh((T_c-core_temperature_set_point)/feedback_recruitment_temperature_scale) varies little and the law approaches a single approximately linear restorative relation after local refitting.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: With ambient_temperature, basal_heat_production, environmental_heat_transfer_coefficient, and effective_heat_capacity held fixed, plotting dT_c_dt against T_c shows an approximately linear relation near core_temperature_set_point but increasingly steeper cooling for larger positive T_c-core_temperature_set_point. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only any hidden auxiliary trajectory, and is observable across experiments that differ in initial thermal offset while staying in the mild physiological range.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only produce one affine dependence of dT_c_dt on T_c, so after matching near-set-point relaxation it necessarily underpredicts the stronger restoration seen at larger deviations, or after matching large-deviation recovery it overpredicts the local slope near the set point. This mismatch persists across trajectories with different initial offsets under the same ambient conditions because the child changes curvature of the target mapping rather than merely rescaling one coefficient.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed effective_heat_capacity, the same net heat flux always produces a temperature-rate change with constant conversion factor, so dT_c_dt is affine in net heat flux apart from the existing feedback nonlinearity.
response_change.child_relation: Make effective thermal storage depend on core temperature so the same net heat flux yields different dT_c_dt at different T_c, changing the local slope and curvature of the T_c-to-dT_c_dt map even when ambient conditions and activity are fixed.
response_change.observable_effect: For comparable positive and negative thermal deviations around the set point, recovery becomes asymmetric in speed: regions with larger effective heat capacity show slower temperature-rate response to the same restoring heat flux magnitude.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when admissible core-temperature excursions are large enough that temperature-dependent tissue heat storage is not negligible relative to the baseline effective_heat_capacity variation scale, while remaining in mild physiological ranges with positive total heat capacity.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, small perturbations near set point can still look close to the parent law; in holdout with somewhat larger but still physiological excursions, the altered temperature-rate curvature appears as systematically slower or faster relaxation than any one constant-capacity fit predicts.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the temperature dependence of effective heat capacity to zero, giving a constant effective_heat_capacity.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Temperature-dependent effective heat capacity from changing partition of stored heat among tissues and body water over mild thermal deviations.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the coefficient converting net heat flux into temperature rate now varies with the evolving state T_c, changing local slope and curvature across the trajectory rather than globally rescaling the response.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Effective heat capacity is constant over the modeled range.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Effective heat capacity increases smoothly with squared normalized deviation of core temperature from the set point while remaining positive over mild physiological excursions.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when heat_capacity_temperature_sensitivity = 0, so the denominator becomes the constant effective_heat_capacity.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Holding ambient_temperature, basal_heat_production, environmental_heat_transfer_coefficient, and thermoregulatory_feedback_gain fixed while varying initial perturbation amplitude, near-set-point trajectories remain close to the parent but larger admissible excursions show reduced |dT_c_dt| because the state-dependent denominator increases with |T_c - core_temperature_set_point|. evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally reproduce both small-error and larger-error recovery rates across these conditions because the parent has one constant flux-to-temperature-rate conversion factor. response_change.parent_relation: The thermoregulatory correction is an instantaneous static function of the current core-temperature error, so for any observed T_c the target dT_c_dt is uniquely determined with no dependence on recent thermal history.
response_change.child_relation: The corrective thermoeffector drive is generated by a first-order lagged internal state that tracks core-temperature error, so the same observed T_c can yield different dT_c_dt depending on whether the system is early or late in recovery after the perturbation.
response_change.observable_effect: After a step-like thermal perturbation, early-time relaxation is weaker than the parent predicts and later-time relaxation strengthens at similar T_c, creating hysteresis in the dT_c_dt versus T_c relationship.
